'''Raja Dia Bell'''<ref>{{Cite web|title=Raja Bell welcomes his champion son|url=https://people.com/parents/raja_bell_welco/|access-date=2021-04-19|website=PEOPLE.com|language=en|archive-date=December 5, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221205125119/https://people.com/parents/raja_bell_welco/|url-status=live}}</ref> (born September 19, 1976) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player and podcaster. He played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], [[Dallas Mavericks]], [[Utah Jazz]], [[Phoenix Suns]], [[Charlotte Bobcats]], and [[Golden State Warriors]]. He was twice named to the [[NBA All-Defensive Team]].

Bell spent the 2014–15 season as the director of player development for the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. He is now a podcast host for ''[[The Ringer (website)|The Ringer]]''.

==Early life and college career==
Bell was born on [[Saint Croix, U.S. Virgin Islands|Saint Croix]] in the [[U.S. Virgin Islands]]. He grew up in the greater [[Miami]], Florida, area, attending Ponce de Leon Junior High School, [[Gulliver Academy]], and [[Miami Killian Senior High School]]. He began his college career at [[Boston University]], where he was [[America East Conference]] (then called North Atlantic Conference) Freshman of the Year. After his sophomore year, Bell left Boston University for reasons unrelated to basketball. He transferred to [[Florida International University]] (FIU) in Miami for his junior and senior seasons. Bell went undrafted out of college in the [[1999 NBA draft]].

==Professional playing career==
===Yakima Sun Kings (1999–2000)===
Bell began his professional career with the [[Yakima Sun Kings]] of the [[Continental Basketball Association]] (CBA). He won a [[CBA champion|CBA championship]] with the Sun Kings in 2000.<ref>{{cite web |title=1999-00 Yakima Sun Kings Statistics |url=https://www.statscrew.com/minorbasketball/stats/t-CBAYSK/y-1999 |website=Stats Crew |access-date=March 12, 2025 |archive-date=March 12, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250312154213/https://www.statscrew.com/minorbasketball/stats/t-CBAYSK/y-1999 |url-status=live }}</ref> He was selected to the CBA All-Rookie Team in 2000.<ref>{{cite web |title=Raja Bell minor league basketball statistics |url=https://www.statscrew.com/minorbasketball/stats/p-bellraj001 |website=Stats Crew |access-date=July 13, 2021 |archive-date=July 13, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210713104244/https://www.statscrew.com/minorbasketball/stats/p-bellraj001 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Philadelphia 76ers (2001–2002)===
Bell signed as a [[free agent]] with the [[San Antonio Spurs]] on August 2, 2000, but never played a game for them. He was eventually released, and then signed the first of two 10 day contracts with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] on April 6, 2001. Bell later signed a contract for the rest of the season after the two 10 day contracts expired. He played limited minutes in the final five of the Sixers' games in the [[2000–01 NBA season|2000–01 regular season]], but saw action in 15 of the team's 23 playoff games. The little-used Bell starred in Game 7 of the 2001 Eastern Conference Finals, scoring 10 points (all in the 2nd quarter) and rallying the Sixers from an early deficit against the Bucks as the 76ers won easily. He played in all five games for the 76ers in the [[2001 NBA Finals]].

Bell played in 74 games with the Sixers in the [[2001–02 NBA season]], averaging 3.4 points per game, and played in three of the team's five playoff games as the Sixers suffered a five-game playoff series loss to the [[Boston Celtics]].

===Dallas Mavericks (2002–2003)===
On October 1, 2002, Bell signed as a free agent with the [[Dallas Mavericks]], and he averaged 3.1 points in 15.6 minutes per game. For the first time in his NBA career, he gained extensive starting experience, starting in 32 of the 75 games he played.

Bell averaged 5.7 points and 3.0 rebounds per game in 17 post-season games with the 2003 Mavericks as the team advanced to the Western Conference Finals.

===Utah Jazz (2003–2005)===
On September 26, 2003, Bell signed with the [[Utah Jazz]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Jazz Agree to terms with Bell |work=[[NBA.com]] |url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/bell_092603.html |date=2003-09-26 |access-date=2009-01-19 |archive-date=January 1, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090101170314/http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/bell_092603.html |url-status=live }}</ref> and enjoyed what had been his most successful season since entering the NBA. Bell played in all 82 of the Jazz's games, and despite starting in only four of them, he posted career highs with 11.2 points, 2.9 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 24.6 minutes per game. In the [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05 season]] he slightly improved upon these stats with 12.3 points, 3.2 rebounds, and 1.4 assists per game, despite playing in only 63 games.

===Phoenix Suns (2005–2008)===
[[File:Rajab.jpg|thumb|150px|left|Bell with the [[Phoenix Suns]] in 2008]]
On August 3, 2005, Bell signed with the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Suns Sign Guard Raja Bell |work=[[NBA.com]] |url=http://www.nba.com/suns/news/bell_050803.html |date=2005-08-03 |access-date=2009-01-19 |archive-date=December 14, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081214062144/http://www.nba.com/suns/news/bell_050803.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Bell responded to the presence of [[Steve Nash]] and became an extremely solid contributor. He started in all 79 games he played in, and finished the 2005–06 season averaging 14.7 points per game in 37.5 minutes per game.

Bell also hit a career high 44.2% of his 3-point field goal attempts during the 2005–06 season. He was chosen to participate in the 2006 NBA Footlocker Three-Point Shootout, but did not participate due to a family illness and was replaced by [[Gilbert Arenas]].

One of the most notable incidents of Bell's career occurred in the [[2006 NBA Playoffs]] on May 2, 2006, in Game 5 of a first round series against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. Bell clotheslined Lakers star guard [[Kobe Bryant]] on a hard foul, resulting in an ejection (with 7:33 left to play in the game).<ref>{{cite news |first=Doug |last=Haller |title=Bell's foul is cause for great concern |url=http://www.azcentral.com/sports/suns/articles/0503sunssidechase0503.html |work=[[The Arizona Republic]] |date=May 3, 2006 |access-date=2007-04-29 |archive-date=May 5, 2006 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060505060155/http://www.azcentral.com/sports/suns/articles/0503sunssidechase0503.html |url-status=live }}</ref> In the postgame press conference, Bell explained that he was retaliating to an elbow to the jaw from Bryant. "It's a personal thing when someone continually hits you in the face... There doesn't seem to be any boundaries or limitations for what he's allowed to do to me, and at that point, I kind of lost my cool and I took it into my own hands." Bell was suspended for one game after his clothesline. The Suns eventually won the series in 7 games.<ref>{{cite news |first=Paul |last=Coro |title=Bell ringers: Raja blasts Kobe |url=http://www.azcentral.com/sports/suns/articles/0504rajasoundsoff-CR.html |work=[[The Arizona Republic]] |date=May 4, 2006 |access-date=2007-04-29 |archive-date=May 6, 2006 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060506063332/http://www.azcentral.com/sports/suns/articles/0504rajasoundsoff-CR.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

During the next round of the [[2006 NBA Playoffs]], Bell demonstrated his clutch abilities in Game 5 with a last second three-pointer in overtime against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] to tie the game and send it into double-overtime, where the Suns eventually pulled away to win and go up 3 to 2 in the series. In Game 1 of the Western Conference Finals against the Dallas Mavericks, midway through the fourth quarter, Bell sustained a calf injury which forced him to miss the rest of the game, as well as the next two games of the series. Bell returned in Game 4 to help the Suns tie the series at two games apiece, though they eventually fell to the Mavericks.

On January 5, 2007, Bell was suspended one game without pay for kicking [[Andrea Bargnani]] in a road game against the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2721535 |title=NBA suspends Bell for kicking Bargnani |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 5, 2007 |access-date=2007-07-31 |archive-date=December 4, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241204165959/https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2721535 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Bell finished the 2006–07 season with 205 total three-point shots made, tying the [[Washington Wizards]]' [[Gilbert Arenas]] for the league lead.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/leagues/NBA_2007_t.html |title=2006–07 NBA Expanded Standings and Leaders |publisher=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=2007-08-04 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070702202106/http://basketball-reference.com/leagues/NBA_2007_t.html <!-- Bot retrieved archive --> |archive-date = 2007-07-02}}</ref><ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/stats/player?season=2007 NBA Player 3-Point Shooting Statistics - 2006-07 (sorted by Three-point Field Goals Made)]</ref>

===Charlotte Bobcats (2008–2009)===
[[File:Raja Bell Bobcats.jpg|thumb|right|Bell with the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] in 2009]]
On December 10, 2008, Bell was traded to the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] along with [[Boris Diaw]] and [[Sean Singletary]] in exchange for [[Jason Richardson]], [[Jared Dudley]] and a [[Gani Lawal|2010 second-round draft pick]] in a move by the Suns to retool their roster.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bobcats Acquire Boris Diaw, Raja Bell and Sean Singletary from Phoenix |work=[[NBA.com]] |url=http://www.nba.com/bobcats/081210_bobcats_trade.html |date=2008-12-10 |access-date=2008-12-11 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081213232926/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/081210_bobcats_trade.html |archive-date=2008-12-13 }}</ref> This came after a disappointing start to the season for Bell during which he posted just 9.6 points per game and saw a diminished role under new coach [[Terry Porter]].

===Golden State Warriors (2009–2010)===
On November 16, 2009, Bell was traded to the [[Golden State Warriors]] along with [[Vladimir Radmanović]] in exchange for [[Stephen Jackson]] and [[Acie Law]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Warriors Acquire Bell & Radmanovic From Charlotte | work=NBA.com | url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors_acquire_bell_radmanovic_111609.html | date=2009-11-16 | access-date=2009-11-16 | archive-date=November 19, 2009 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091119001920/http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors_acquire_bell_radmanovic_111609.html | url-status=live }}</ref> He played just one game for the Warriors; in his lone performance scoring 11 points while hitting all three of his three-point attempts.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/49/raja-bell |title=Raja Bell Game Log - Utah Jazz - ESPN (2009-10) |access-date=July 16, 2024 |archive-date=February 23, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250223003635/https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/49/raja-bell |url-status=live }}</ref> He was released from the team on March 22, 2010.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/williams_signed_bell_waived_032210.html | title=Warriors Sign Reggie Williams For Remainder of Season | work=[[NBA.com]] | date=2010-03-22 | access-date=2010-03-23 | archive-date=March 25, 2010 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100325012402/http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/williams_signed_bell_waived_032210.html | url-status=live }}</ref> Bell's trade to the Warriors notably cleared the way for [[Stephen Curry|Steph Curry]] to be the long-term point guard for Golden State, as he had previously been benched for Acie Law.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.gq.com/story/my-rookie-season-stephen-curry-on-the-stephen-jackson-acie-law-trade| title=My Rookie Season: Stephen Curry on the Stephen Jackson / Acie Law Trade| work=[[NBA.com]]| date=2010-03-22| access-date=2010-03-23| archive-date=February 28, 2024| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240228160022/https://www.gq.com/story/my-rookie-season-stephen-curry-on-the-stephen-jackson-acie-law-trade| url-status=live}}</ref>

===Return to Utah (2010–2013)===
On July 14, 2010, Bell signed a three-year, $10 million contract to return to the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite news | title=Raja Bell to Utah, not LA | work=NBA.com | url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/la-sp-lakers-raja-bell-20100715,0,2460431.story | date=2010-07-15 | access-date=2010-07-15 | first=Mike | last=Bresnahan | archive-date=July 18, 2010 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100718232511/http://www.latimes.com/sports/la-sp-lakers-raja-bell-20100715,0,2460431.story | url-status=live }}</ref> However, his relationship with the team soured after two seasons.  In a mutual agreement, he spent much of the 2012–13 season away from the team while still under contract.<ref>{{cite news|last=Pincus|first=Eric|title=Utah Jazz executive talks Raja Bell and the Lakers|date=February 26, 2013|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/lakersnow/la-sp-ln-utah-jazz-executive-raja-bell-lakers-20130226,0,843608.story|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130227225725/http://www.latimes.com/sports/lakersnow/la-sp-ln-utah-jazz-executive-raja-bell-lakers-20130226,0,843608.story|archive-date=February 27, 2013|url-status=live}}</ref> On March 10, 2013, Bell was waived by the Jazz.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-waives-guard-raja-bell | title=Jazz Waives Guard Raja Bell | work=NBA.com | date=2013-03-10 | access-date=2013-03-10 | archive-date=March 13, 2013 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130313024411/http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-waives-guard-raja-bell | url-status=live }}</ref>

===Retirement===
On February 13, 2014, Bell announced his retirement from basketball.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/231925/Raja-Bell-Retires-From-NBA |title=Raja Bell Retires From NBA |access-date=February 14, 2014 |archive-date=February 22, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222134057/http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/231925/Raja-Bell-Retires-From-NBA |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Post-playing career==

=== Executive ===
On October 1, 2014, the Cleveland Cavaliers announced the hiring of Bell as the team's Director of Player Administration.<ref>{{cite tweet|user=JerryZgoda|author=Jerry Zgoda|number=561661892264218625|date=31 January 2015|title=Kevin Love in the house}}/photo/1</ref> He left the role in September, 2015, citing a desire to spend more time with his family. <ref>{{Cite web |title=Daily News - September 15, 2015 |url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/press/daily-news-september-15-2015 |access-date=2024-03-22 |website=www.nba.com |language=en |archive-date=March 22, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240322044915/https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/press/daily-news-september-15-2015 |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Sports media ===
In August 2020, Bell began hosting episodes of ''[[The Ringer (website)|The Ringer]] NBA Show'' with Logan Murdock.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Murdock|first=Logan|date=2020-08-03|title=Reporting on the Bubble With Raja Bell|url=https://www.theringer.com/2020/8/3/21352392/reporting-on-the-bubble-with-raja-bell|access-date=2020-10-05|website=The Ringer|language=en|archive-date=October 9, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201009161158/https://www.theringer.com/2020/8/3/21352392/reporting-on-the-bubble-with-raja-bell|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Personal life and family==
In July 2004, Bell married his girlfriend, Cindy Greenman. On May 2, 2007, Cindy gave birth to their first child, Dia, by [[c-section]] six hours before tip-off of Game 5 against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in the 1st round of the [[2007 NBA Playoffs]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.celebrity-babies.com/2007/05/raja_bell_welco.html |title=Raja Bell welcomes his champion son : Celebrity Baby Blog<!-- Bot generated title --> |access-date=May 6, 2007 |archive-date=December 21, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081221071205/http://www.celebrity-babies.com/2007/05/raja_bell_welco.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> The Suns won that game 119–110, closing the series at 4–1. His wife gave birth to another child, Tai Brooklyn, on November 8, 2008.{{Citation needed|date=June 2021}} 

Bell has one sibling, [[Tombi Bell]], a former WNBA basketball player who attended the [[Florida Gators women's basketball|University of Florida]] and is a former assistant coach of the [[Miami Hurricanes women's basketball|Miami Hurricanes women's basketball team]].

Bell has been a [[Vegetarianism|vegetarian]] since the age of 2.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.azcentral.com/sports/columns/articles/06210622p2main0622.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120720184729/http://www.azcentral.com/sports/columns/articles/06210622p2main0622.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=20 July 2012 |title=Raja's beef? There is none |date=21 June 2007 |first=Bob |last=Young |work=[[The Arizona Republic]] |access-date=4 August 2007}}</ref>

On June 17, 2024, Raja's son, Dia, announced his commitment to play football for the [[Texas Longhorns football|University of Texas at Austin]]. He is one of the top quarterbacks in the 2026 high school recruiting rankings.

=== Social media ===
In 2014, Bell began posting on Instagram under the username Rajadia19, a verified account.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Raja Bell (@rajadia19) • Instagram photos and videos |url=https://www.instagram.com/rajadia19/ |access-date=2022-07-12 |website=www.instagram.com |language=en}}</ref>

In July 2020, Bell created a Twitter account with the username RajaBell19,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://twitter.com/bell19raja |access-date=2023-08-13 |url-access=limited |title=Register |via=[[Twitter]] |language=en |archive-date=May 18, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220518201550/https://twitter.com/bell19raja |url-status=live }}</ref> a nod to the number he wore most often as an NBA player.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Raja Bell Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/bellra01.html |access-date=2022-07-12 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en |archive-date=November 19, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121119042355/http://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/bellra01.html |url-status=live }}</ref> As of early July 2022, more than two years of actively campaigning, Raja has not received verification from Twitter.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Murdock |first=Logan |date=2022-07-11 |title=Summer League Vibes |url=https://www.theringer.com/2022/7/11/23204309/summer-league-vibes |access-date=2022-07-12 |website=The Ringer |language=en |archive-date=July 11, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220711235929/https://www.theringer.com/2022/7/11/23204309/summer-league-vibes |url-status=live }}</ref>
